MODEL EVALUATION · REPRODUCIBLE PUBLIC EXAMPLE

Can a price-direction model beat a simple baseline?

Five-session up/down classification uses lagged returns, historical volatility, and drawdown. An expanding-window L2 logistic regression is tested on later, non-overlapping windows against a past positive-return-frequency baseline. The chart below runs the same implementation on generated example prices; it is not evidence of stock-market accuracy.

Computing a reproducible synthetic test…

Lower Brier score means smaller squared forecast error. The exploratory model score is uncalibrated; neither classification accuracy nor a good synthetic result demonstrates a profitable strategy. Transaction costs, different market regimes, historical issuer selection, and dividends require separate validation.

Methods and mathematical implementation

Algorithms · checks · source code

Each method connects an input, a calculation, and a validation check. Reported company disclosures and market-price observations are distinguished from assumptions and simulated public examples.

01 / FINANCIAL STATEMENT ANALYSIS

Growth, profitability, and cash generation

Revenue growth = Revenueₜ / Revenueₜ₋₁ − 1 Operating margin = Operating income / Revenue FCF proxy = Cash from operations − PP&E purchases

Annual company-facts records are selected by issuer, fiscal period, filing metadata and metric units. Calculated measures are displayed only when the required reported inputs exist.

Checks: fiscal-year ordering, source lineage, negative cash flow, null values and mismatched filing periods.

SEC calculation source · Tests

02 / PORTFOLIO STATISTICS

Covariance and risk estimation

rₜ = Pₜ / Pₜ₋₁ − 1 Portfolio variance = wᵀΣw Annual volatility = sd(r) × √sessions/year

Price observations are aligned before return calculations. The optimizer applies covariance stabilization and evaluates portfolio variance under feasible investment-weight limits.

Checks: price validity, matching dates, covariance symmetry, positive variance and valid annualization conventions.

Optimizer source · Tests

03 / NUMERICAL OPTIMIZATION

Constrained allocation

Minimize wᵀΣw subject to Σwᵢ = 1 and 0 ≤ wᵢ ≤ cap

Optimized portfolios are compared against an equal-weight baseline. Cap constraints and objective feasibility are validated before reporting results.

Checks: sum-to-one, cap compliance, infeasible constraints, objective-value reconciliation and comparison against the fitted baseline.

Implementation · Tests

04 / OUT-OF-SAMPLE TIME SERIES

Walk-forward strategy evaluation

Fit on times 1…T → evaluate on T+1…T+h Net wealth = gross wealth − modeled trading costs

The evaluation separates past-only training windows from later test periods, compares allocation rules on matched windows, and tracks fees, drawdowns and sensitivity to modeling choices.

Checks: no future-data leakage, nonoverlapping test periods, fee reconciliation, passive baseline and leave-one-window-out sensitivity.

Robustness implementation · Tests

05 / DISCOUNTED CASH FLOW

Scenario sensitivity and terminal-value exposure

FCFₜ = Revenue₀ × (1 + g)ᵗ × assumed margin PV = Σ [FCFₜ/(1+r)ᵗ] + TV/(1+r)ᴺ

SEC financials define the observed baseline; growth, margin, terminal assumptions and discounting are explicit scenario inputs. Terminal-value share measures sensitivity of the modeled proxy.

Checks: discount-rate bounds, missing cash-flow inputs, terminal share and changing growth/discount assumptions. This proxy is not a verified stock-price target.

Input-integrity source · Tests

06 / REPRODUCIBILITY & MODEL RISK

Provenance, regression testing, and failure cases

Evidence = {source, date range, settings, model version, results, dataset fingerprint, checks}

Historical observation windows, configurable assumptions, source provenance and SHA-256 fingerprints support reproducible comparisons. Automated Python and JavaScript regression tests exercise expected results and reject invalid inputs.

Checks: changed-data fingerprint, stale data, missing values, private-data exclusion, SEC period integrity and Python 3.11/3.12 CI. “Regression tests” here means software tests; it does not imply an implemented OLS return-prediction model.

Python tests · JavaScript tests

From result to interpretation

Models provide estimates conditional on data and assumptions. The research workflow compares independent evidence (company fundamentals, observed return history, diversification, out-of-sample behavior and scenario sensitivity), identifies disagreement, and documents what remains uncertain. Model fit or a high ranking is not sufficient evidence of an investable advantage.

Implementation and test references

Algorithms · diagnostics · engineering judgment
QUANTITATIVE FINANCE / NUMERICAL OPTIMIZATION

01. Constrained portfolio optimization

Allocation weights are fitted from observed returns and an estimated covariance matrix, subject to feasibility and concentration limits.

Implemented privately
min wᵀΣw   subject to   Σwᵢ = 1;   0 ≤ wᵢ ≤ cap

Why it matters: the objective is predicted portfolio variance, not a guarantee of realized return. The private optimizer supports a covariance-based minimum-risk allocation and alternative inverse-volatility / return-tilt allocations.

  • Align price histories to comparable observations before estimating returns.
  • Apply covariance stabilization/shrinkage and reject impossible weight caps.
  • Compare annualized volatility, drawdown, tail loss and alternative allocations.
Implementation and verification detail

Estimated portfolio volatility is √(wᵀΣw) × √annualization; optimization remains sensitive to return sampling, correlated assets and constraints. Tests check symmetry, finite prices, positive covariance diagonals, feasibility and weight normalization.

Schematic risk vs. return trade-off

Illustrative positions, not an empirical efficient frontier or a private portfolio result.

STATISTICAL VALIDATION / TIME SERIES

02. Rolling walk-forward evaluation

A model trains on past observations, then is evaluated on the following unseen sessions. The allocation is refitted at later boundaries.

Implemented privately
Train[t₀:t₁] → Fit w₁ → Test[t₁:t₂] → Roll forward

The private study supports non-overlapping evaluation windows, modeled turnover and basis-point transaction fees, two rebalanced strategies, and a passive equal-weight buy-and-hold comparison.

  • Run each allocation rule against matched evaluation dates.
  • Reconcile per-window fees to total reported costs.
  • Perform leave-one-window-out diagnostics; a changed winner signals sample dependence.
  • Preserve observations and model settings in versioned research manifests.
Where bias can still enter

Past-only fitting reduces mechanical look-ahead within the test, but cannot eliminate survivorship bias, post-hoc asset selection or tuning parameters after seeing outcomes. Omitting a window without refitting is a sensitivity check, not independent validation.

FINANCIAL MODELING / SEC DISCLOSURES

03. SEC-backed forecast sensitivity

Observed company financials are kept distinct from hypothetical revenue-growth, cash-flow-margin and discounting assumptions.

Real source + modeled scenarios
FCFₜ = Revenue₀(1+g)ᵗ × margin
PV = Σ FCFₜ/(1+r)ᵗ + TV/(1+r)ᴺ

Real SEC annual statements establish the observed baseline. The model projects three- to seven-year hypothetical scenarios and produces a sensitivity grid for revenue growth and the discount rate.

  • Report free cash-flow proxy as operating cash flow less cash PP&E purchases.
  • Distinguish discounted cash-flow proxy from an equity value or share-price target.
  • Display how much present value comes from the terminal component.
  • Reject impossible assumptions and missing SEC cash flows instead of fabricating data.
Terminal-value risk

Terminal value extrapolates cash flows beyond the explicit projection horizon. When the terminal share dominates, small changes in discount and perpetual growth rates can materially change the result. Debt, excess cash and capital-structure adjustments are not included in this proxy.

How scenarios respond to assumptions

ChangeEffect on modeled proxy
Higher assumed revenue growthUsually higher
Higher assumed FCF marginHigher
Higher discount rateLower
Higher terminal growth (r > g)Usually higher

Directional sensitivities are mathematical examples, not measured company forecast accuracy. Real reported values are available in SEC Financials.

DATA SCIENCE / EXPLAINABLE RESEARCH

04. Historical investment screening

A private shortlist compares price momentum, realized volatility and drawdown, while displaying available SEC fundamentals separately.

Owner-only research
Score = Σ (lens weightₖ × normalized metricₖ)

Growth, balanced and risk-aware lenses change how much weight the model places on trailing return, recent momentum, annualized volatility and historical drawdown. The score is an explainable heuristic, not a probability of gain.

  • Use selectable investment names rather than requiring ticker memorization.
  • Flag sparse histories and report the period and IEX/SIP source.
  • Show SEC revenue growth and FCF margins only when disclosed facts support them.
  • Keep ranking and trade execution separate; no brokerage orders are placed.
Why a top-ranked investment may still be unattractive

Momentum and low observed volatility do not measure whether a stock is expensive relative to its future cash flows. Future returns also depend on valuation, concentration, news and unforeseeable events. The research lens is for comparing candidates, not picking guaranteed winners.

Explainability layers

EvidencePrice history, volatility, drawdown and optional SEC context
ScoreWeighted, bounded and traceable to its inputs
LimitsSelection bias, changing regimes, price-only returns
DecisionManual research and hypothetical portfolio workflow, not an order

The private browser uses real historical observations when authorized; no private rankings or selected holdings are displayed here.

Research integrity and engineering controls

Reproducibility + security
Source lineage

Issuer and fiscal-year filtering, filings and cutoffs, calendar alignment, adjusted-provider-price attribution and unavailable-value handling.

Reproducible manifests

Versioned exports include investment symbols, settings, evaluation dates, fee rules and SHA-256 input fingerprints; raw licensed prices are not exported.

Testable calculations

Python and JavaScript tests include invalid prices, impossible allocation caps, missing filings, look-ahead prevention, fee reconciliation and prior-window comparisons.

Release gates

GitHub Actions checks Python 3.11 and 3.12, the private regression suites, privacy review, script syntax and compiled Content Security Policy hashes.

PUBLICCloudflare PagesReal SEC snapshot and labeled browser-only illustrative models
EDGEScoped API proxyRestricted configured upstream; private backend credentials not returned
PRIVATE APIRender / FastAPIAuthorized requests for market observations and personal state
IDENTITY & DATASupabase MFAAuthenticator step-up and owner-scoped virtual account records

The diagrams document intended and tested boundaries, not a claim that any production system is immune to attack. SHA-256 fingerprints detect changed in-memory inputs but do not authenticate the provider or replace archived source data.

LayerExample invariantsWhy it matters
Historical dataFinite positive prices; aligned time series; observed-versus-derived SEC metricsRejects inconsistent or fabricated model inputs

Live browser acceptance checklist (not yet independently verified)

Automated tests and Cloudflare HTML verification cannot prove that authenticated provider workflows work. Complete these steps in a real browser, without sharing credentials or brokerage account data.

  1. Sign in and complete MFA from a fresh private session.
  2. Open Portfolio and confirm authorized holdings and market quotes load without an error.
  3. Select 2–5 companies by name, load matching market data, and run one complete Decision Center assessment.
  4. Confirm built-in SEC fundamentals work in standard research. If testing the optional local filing archive, inspect withheld dates in Advanced Research.
  5. Open Research Lab and Briefing; confirm consistent candidate, model counts, and evidence status.
  6. Save and delete a research archive note, then sign out and confirm protected data disappear. Test persistence after a separate sign-in.

These are manual tests; this checklist does not automatically mark them passed.

Finance terms · plain-English reference

Volatility: how much prices moved up and down in the observed period.

Drawdown: how far a portfolio fell from a prior high.

Backtest: a calculation using past prices, not proof of future success.

Walk-forward: a backtest that repeatedly fits on earlier data and checks later observations.

Cash flow: money reported moving through a company; this is not the same as stock-price return.

Concentration: how dependent your portfolio value is on one holding.

SEC filing: a company disclosure filed with the US securities regulator.

FCF proxy: operating cash flow minus cash spent on property and equipment; not a stock-price target.

Discount rate: a model assumption about the value of future cash flow in today’s dollars.

Correlation: how two observed return series moved together; historical correlation can change.

Before acting: a research checklist
  1. Can I explain what the company or fund owns and how it makes money?
  2. Are my financial figures reported, current, and comparable across periods?
  3. What do the historical risk and walk-forward results disagree about?
  4. How would this change concentration or cash in my portfolio?
  5. What information is still missing, and would a possible loss affect money I need soon?

Use the analysis links in your generated report to answer each question. This is a review tool, not a buy/sell signal.

This is a rule-based research explanation, not a generative AI chatbot, investment recommendation, or personalized suitability determination. Nothing is sent to an AI service.

HISTORICAL DECISION SUPPORT

Screening summary

Summarizes comparative measures, overlap with existing holdings, and unresolved risks. Historical ranks are not trade recommendations.

Reading the scores

A higher research score indicates a more favorable balance of past momentum and realized risk under the selected lens. It is not an estimated probability of profit, expected return, or price target. SEC results describe past business finances separately; ETFs generally do not have comparable company income statements. Reassess against valuation, diversification, fees, tax impact, investment horizon, and the risk of loss before any real-money decision. IEX-only bars are not consolidated market-wide prices.

Historical prices and risk

Load daily stock, ETF, or supported USD cryptocurrency prices from the private Alpaca connection. Equity prices are price-only, excluding dividends; cryptocurrency trades seven days a week.

Check the Research investments panel above for selected symbols, loaded observations, and date coverage.

Load a historical series to begin.

Optimize an allocation

Use the loaded historical returns to calculate long-only weights subject to concentration limits. Review correlations and risk contributions before interpreting the proposed allocation. Results do not alter your virtual holdings.

Select 2–5 investments in Market data, load their history, then calculate an allocation.

Risk diagnostics

Risk estimates use historical returns and a 20% diagonal covariance shrinkage. Correlations, drawdowns, and tail-loss statistics describe the selected sample; they do not predict future outcomes.

Risk diagnostics appear after an allocation is calculated.

Buy-and-hold vs. rebalancing

Compare equal-weight buy-and-hold and monthly rebalancing on the loaded historical price series, after modeled transaction fees. These are retrospective calculations, not an executable trading record.

Walk-forward strategy comparison

Fit portfolio weights on earlier prices and evaluate on subsequent periods, refitting at each boundary. Compare against equal-weight rebalancing using the same transaction-fee assumptions. No brokerage orders.

Load price history in Market data to begin.

Performance and risk diagnostics

Benchmark and sensitivity checks

Compare a passive benchmark, alternative weight rules, larger fees, and leave-one-window-out sensitivity on matched evaluation dates. Select a longer history in Research investments and reload if the analysis has too few test windows.

Run Walk-forward first, then check robustness.

Model uses price-only historical returns; no dividends, borrow costs, slippage, taxes, or corporate-action simulations. Backtests remain subject to selection bias and do not establish future performance.

SEC-based valuation scenarios

Start with company cash-flow disclosures and vary growth, discount, and terminal-value assumptions. Alpaca prices are separate market observations, not accounting data. Scenario values are not price targets.
